title: Healthcheck route
idea: A healthcheck route is an endpoint that answers 200 when the server is running, so people and tools can check it without logging in.
points: A load balancer, which spreads traffic across servers, polls it; so do uptime monitors.
The controller is a function `(req, res)` that sends `new ApiResponse(200, data, message)`.
The router maps `GET /` to that controller; `route('/')` lets you chain more methods.
`app.use('/api/v1/healthcheck', router)` mounts it; the router sees only the rest of the path.

messages.label: GET /api/v1/healthcheck
messages.note: `app.use` matches the path prefix and hands the request to the healthcheck router.

messages.label: path is now /
messages.note: Express strips the mount prefix, so the router sees only `/`.

messages.label: healthCheck(req, res)
messages.note: `route('/').get` matches the method and path, then calls the controller.

messages.label: new ApiResponse(200, …)
messages.note: The controller builds the standard response object.

messages.label: 200 + JSON
messages.note: `res.json` sends it. The client gets `statusCode`, `data`, `message` and `success`.

messages.label: POST /api/v1/healthcheck
messages.note: A different method on the same path.
The router has no `POST` route, so Express falls through to its built-in 404.

code.title: Three files in one run
code.caption: Each commented block is one project file. This copy calls itself, then closes.

walk.text: `ApiResponse` from earlier: every success reply gets the same shape.
The controller sends `200` and an `ApiResponse` as JSON. It does no async work.
A router holds the routes. `route('/')` is the path inside the mount point.
`app.use` mounts the router. The full URL is the prefix plus `/`.
Listen on a free port and build the test URL.
`GET` reaches the controller: status 200 and the JSON body.
`POST` has no route, so Express answers with its built-in 404.

pitfalls: Do not treat `200` as proof the database works; this route never queries it.
Return no secrets or internal details: the route is public.
Remember the mount prefix: a router's `/` is `/api/v1/healthcheck`, not the site root.

quiz.why: Only `GET` is registered. A `POST` matches no route, so Express answers 404, not 405.

takeaway: The controller replies, the router maps the path, `app.use` mounts it.

starters: Why does the path start with `/api/v1`?
How would a healthcheck that tests the database look?
What is the difference between `router.route('/').get` and `router.get('/')`?
